title: Losing your driver licence (suspension)
summary: This page provides information on why a driver licence might be suspended and what steps to take regarding the suspension and appeal process.

Understanding of the appeal process and deadlines (e.g., 28 days for police suspension).

If selling a vehicle, you may need to cancel the vehicle registration and reserve number plates.

faqs.q: Why might my driver licence be suspended?
faqs.a: Suspension can occur for several reasons, including exceeding your demerit points limit, not paying outstanding fines, medical reasons, or committing a traffic offence (such as car, rider, or heavy vehicle offences).

faqs.q: What happens if I receive an on-the-spot suspension from the police?
faqs.a: If the suspension is on the spot, it begins immediately, and you cannot drive away; someone else must pick up your vehicle. If it happens within 48 hours of being charged, the suspension may be automatic (3 or 6 months) or remain in place until your case is heard by a court.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a licence suspension?
faqs.a: You must file your appeal within 28 days of the date you were suspended. You can find specific guidance on appealing the suspension or cancellation for medical reasons, or generally appealing the suspension.

faqs.q: When can I drive again after a suspension?
faqs.a: You may be able to drive again if you buy a driving record online, call 13 77 88, visit a Service NSW Centre, successfully appeal the suspension, or are found not guilty in court.
